prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: transparent terrain sprite atlas for a low-resolution strategy-map rendering experiment.
Input images: the two supplied local screenshot crops are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY, especially their low sweeping lime-green ridges, dark green slope wedges, cream-lit angular rock faces. Do not reproduce any buildings, characters, trees or UI.
Primary request: Create ONE carefully aligned 4-column by 4-row sprite sheet of SIXTEEN SEPARATE COMPLETE terrain objects, every object fully inside its own equally sized square cell. Transparent outside each object, NO background, no ground tile, no checkerboard painted into the art. Use a square canvas. Every object centered horizontally in its cell, its bottom ground-contact at 85 percent of cell height. Leave transparent padding around all four sides of each object; at least 10 percent horizontal cell padding. No grid lines or dividers, no text.
Rows in order:
Row 1: four different very broad LOW GRASSY HILLS, one dominant gently bent crest, 4 to 5 times as wide as their height. Long shallow toes on both sides. Vary left-heavy, right-heavy, flattened crest and round arch.
Row 2: four different larger grass-covered FOOTHILLS, 3 to 4 times as wide as their height. One asymmetrical crest and one continuous body. Sweeping thick inset yellow-lime band on upper-left slope, middle grass plane and a broad dark moss-green near/right flank. Different bend and shoulder width per object.
Row 3: four different GREEN FOOTHILLS WITH SMALL EMBEDDED GRAY ROCK TEETH below the grassy crest, gray rock covering 20 to 35 percent of the silhouette. One complete landform each, not a row of little humps. Long grassy lower slopes, no outlined pedestal.
Row 4: four different complete ANGULAR ROCK MOUNTAINS with pointed off-center summits and 2 to 3 branching buttresses on the same coherent mountain. Their height roughly 60 to 80 percent of their full width. Warm cream-lit left ridges, medium-gray faces, dark charcoal-gray gullies and right faces. Broad green low skirts on both sides. Pale stone follows faces all the way down; it is NOT snow.
Shared style: upright strategy-map terrain viewed from high above with visible front slopes, not isometric, no diamond footprint. Match the screenshot style: big connected stepped pixel clusters, yellow-lime grassy crests, olive-green slopes, continuous deep green shadow wedge; warm pale rock highlights and cool neutral rock shadows. Upper-left light for EVERY object. No rim stroke around the green base, no outline oval, no foundation, no floating island, no grass tufts or scattered pixels, no detached cast shadows. Both left and right feet always completely included. Low wide landforms designed to overlap into a continuous range.
Constraints: Sixteen independent silhouettes in a precise 4x4 grid, TRANSPARENT outside silhouettes. No touching neighboring cells. Keep the same lighting and palette throughout. No text, labels, numbers, watermark, icons, buildings, rivers, trees, people, sky or horizon.
STYLE A: very graphic cartoon pixel art. Emphasize simplicity: only 3 broad grassy shading regions and 3 rock shading regions. Deliberate chunky pixels, logical per-cell sprite scale about 32 by 32 native pixels, large stepped edge runs, minimal internal marks. Rich bright yellow-lime crests, dark moss-green lower-right slopes. Bold smooth hill proportions.
